title: [YouPass Collect] - Youth unemployment rates in European countries
prompt: The graph below illustrates the unemployment rates among people aged 15 to 24 in five European countries in 2005, compared to the overall unemployment percentages in those countries. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart compares the percentage of unemployed young people aged 15 to 24 with the overall unemployment rate across five European nations in 2005.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, youth unemployment exceeded the general unemployment rate in all five countries surveyed. Additionally, Poland recorded the highest figures for both categories, while Denmark had the lowest proportions in both cases.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding countries with higher unemployment levels, Poland topped the list with 37% of young people being unemployed, which was more than double the country's overall unemployment rate of 15%. Italy followed with 23% youth unemployment, nearly three times higher than its overall figure of 8%. Similarly, Hungary reported that 17% of its young population was unemployed, compared to just 7% for the general workforce, representing a difference of 10 percentage points.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the remaining nations, Germany's youth unemployment stood at 14%, only 4 percentage points higher than the country's overall rate of 10%. Meanwhile, Denmark recorded the most favorable figures among the five countries, with youth unemployment at 7% and overall unemployment at just 3%, representing both the lowest rates and the smallest gap between the two categories across all surveyed nations.
